subject: Private deployment: Mediplus on-prem audit & egress asks — exec approval request
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sita Rao <sita.rao@mediplus.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment: Mediplus initial SOW + asks (audit / egress / discount)

Hi Sita / Anil —

Great to connect last week. Attached is the updated SOW and the pricing grid for the on-prem pilot we discussed. TL;DR of the Mediplus asks that need internal alignment: 

- Full in-country install (APAC region) with customer-controlled network (on-prem appliance).
- No external egress of raw logs or payloads permitted; customer requests a permanent egress block except for a 6‑hour forensic window upon formal request.
- Broad audit rights: Mediplus legal requests host-level access and the ability to run independent forensic audits on the node during the pilot.
- Managed KMS/HSM is acceptable but Mediplus wants a “bring-your-own-key” flow with full retention controls.
- Commercial: they are asking for 40% platform discount + waived setup fees for a 3‑year committed reserved capacity.

We need: (a) Deal desk / exec approval on discount and (b) legal/infra guidance on whether we can grant host access / permanent egress block / audit scope and suggested contract language.

Attachments: Mediplus_SOW_v3.pdf; DL-2026-1137-pricing-grid.xlsx

Next steps: I want to escalate to Lauren for commercial clearance if we can’t find an acceptable compromise quickly. Karthik, can you confirm the commercial levers we can offer? Irene, legal/ops input appreciated on the host access & audit asks.

Thanks —
Mina
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: Mediplus initial SOW + asks (audit / egress / discount)

Mina / team —

Thanks for flagging. Quick commercial read: 40% on a three-year commit + waived setup is outside our standard tiering for private/Dedicated deals. Typical max concession we've allowed historically for similar risk profiles is 30% on a 2‑year reservation with a non-refundable upfront and an ops onboarding fee.

If we are being asked to accept a permanent egress block and host access, that increases our operational and legal exposure materially — that would justify asking for a larger commercial buffer (higher price or longer term) rather than a deeper discount.

Mitigations we can propose that might get closer to the customer ask without fully exposing us:
- Offer 35% discount (midpoint) if they: commit 3 years, accept a 72‑hour forensics window (instead of 6 hours permanent), and pay onboarding+ops cradle fee.
- Replace host-level access with: timeboxed, audited, and witnessed forensic snapshots delivered by an independent third‑party approved by both parties.
- Managed BYOK with HSM but we require key escrow options for emergency support (documented and limited).

If management will not sign off on the host access / permanent egress blockade we should propose the witnessed-forensics + strict egress rules at the application-layer rather than true network-level egress block.

Irene — can you draft the minimum legal guardrails for the witnessed forensic option? If Lauren signs off commercially we can use the above as an offer.

Karthik
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: Mediplus initial SOW + asks (audit / egress / discount)

Team —

Legal / Security take (high level): we cannot grant unrestricted host-level access or a permanent, unconditional egress block without (1) a signed indemnity that covers forensic actions and OS-level changes, (2) strict scope and timeboxing for audits, and (3) a set of security controls that prevent lateral movement or data exfiltration. Specific recommendations: 

1) Audit rights: convert to "evidence and inspection" model. Mediplus can request forensic evidence (logs, sanitized VM snapshots, telemetry) produced by Redwood or an agreed third-party forensics provider. Forensics to be performed under an approved statement of work; any raw disk images or root access require legal signoff and indemnity.

2) Egress: we can accept an application-layer egress prohibition (no telemetry/ML payload exported) enforced by policy and by signed attestations. Network-level permanent egress block introduces product support risk. Instead allow a timebound forensic export (up to 48-72 hours) initiated by Mediplus with pre-approved procedures.

3) BYOK/KMS: BYOK acceptable. We need emergency key-escrow language for recovery limited to specific emergency conditions (court order / legal hold) — preferably escrowed with a neutral custodian.

4) Host access: deny general host shell access. Allowed: remote, recorded sessions in the presence of Mediplus ops + local read-only snapshots provided by Redwood or third‑party. Any root-level operations must be narrowly scoped, documented, and indemnified.

5) Contract drafting points: add audit SOW appendix, forensics runbook reference, clear SLAs on response times, and a security exceptions approval clause that expires after the pilot and must be re-negotiated for production.

If the customer insists on permanent host access we should decline — escalate to Lauren for explicit commercial/legal authorization.

I can draft a redline for the SOW that implements the witnessed-forensics + 72‑hour export and BYOK with escrow. Suggest we use the 35% / 3‑year commercial compromise Karthik proposed as a bargaining chip.

Irene
Head, Legal Ops & Security, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 14:50:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment: Mediplus initial SOW + asks (audit / egress / discount) — request for exec clearance

Lauren —

Escalating for executive signoff. Customer (Mediplus Health) insists on: host-level audit access + permanent egress block + BYOK + 40% discount for a 3‑year on-prem commit. Legal and commercial recommend a compromise: 35% discount for 3 years, witnessed third‑party forensics (72‑hour timeboxed export), BYOK with limited escrow, and deny shell-level host access (only recorded sessions / snapshots).

Why this needs your signoff: granting host-level access or permanent egress block substantially increases operational exposure and would set a precedent for other health vertical deals in APAC. If you approve the compromise below, we will move to final redline and procurement signoff: 

Proposal for Lauren approval (ask):
- Commercial: 35% platform discount, 3‑year reserved commit, onboarding fee applies (one-time).
- Security/Legal: deny host shell access; allow witnessed-forensics via approved third‑party; timeboxed export window of up to 72 hours under SOW; BYOK with limited escrow only for emergencies.
- Contract: include audit SOW appendix, runbook, and security exception that expires at pilot end.

If you approve, please reply-all with an explicit signoff line so I can record in the Deal Desk and push the redline. If you prefer a stricter posture (no discounts / deny any export) also let us know—we’ll take that back to the customer.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1137
Attachments referenced above.

Thanks —
Mina

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment: Mediplus initial SOW + asks (audit / egress / discount) — request for exec clearance

Team —

After reviewing the summary, I approve the compromise approach outlined by Karthik and Irene with the following binding conditions: 

1) Commercial: approve 35% platform discount for DL-2026-1137 on a formal 3‑year reserved capacity commitment, onboarding fee to remain in scope and be non-waived. Finance to record a non-standard discount code and the credit must be contingent on milestone payments (20% upfront).

2) Security/Legal: NO unrestricted host shell access. Forensics to be provided via an agreed third‑party or Redwood-controlled snapshot delivery; any raw disk images require a separate Purchase Order and indemnity. Timeboxed export window capped at 72 hours, and must be requested via the runbook process.

3) BYOK: acceptable with escrow via approved neutral custodian under strict emergency-only conditions; escrow triggers enumerated in the SOW appendix.

4) Pre-conditions: Security checklist must be completed and signed off by Redwood Security (Irene) prior to any OOB (out-of-band) access. Account to sign Redwood's standard indemnity addendum for forensic actions.

5) Documentation: Legal to prepare a redline SOW and an audit appendix; Deal Desk to capture the approval memo and mark the deal as "Exec-cleared — restricted exceptions".

This signoff is time-limited for closing: if contracts are not executed within 30 days this approval expires and any subsequent exception requests must be re-escalated.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Approved: Lauren Bishop (Lauren.Bishop@redwood.ai) — 2026-11-04 09:30 PST
